svg.title: Five Moves Before the First Drawback Claim
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-drawback-claim-launch-sequence; chapter number: 1; title: Five Moves Before the First Drawback Claim; subtitle: From the five-year lookback to a self-run mock audit; caption: Drawback specialists test the opportunity first, then run a shipment trace, clean the export records and stage a mock audit before Customs asks for anything.; assumptions note: The order of steps follows the operator gates and pro-tips the practitioners cited. Customs refunds 99% of eligible duties, taxes and fees and keeps 1%, as International Tariff Management reports.; note: Sources are Evana, Scarlett Jones, the Connecticut District Export Council (Jay Charco), the International Trade Council (Tony Nogueiras) and KPMG US.; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Run the five-year lookback test; value: Step 1; detail: First-time claimants can reach back five years from import. Mid-sized companies that assume drawback is only for big companies find the number gets their CFO's attention (Evana).; step: 02; label: Weigh recovery against filing cost; value: Step 2; detail: If projected recovery does not beat the administrative expense of filing, do not file (Scarlett Jones). Specialist fees start around 10% of recovery (Nogueiras).; step: 03; label: Trace one shipment PO to export; value: Step 3; detail: Trace a single shipment from purchase order to import, through inventory and on to export. Customs grants waiver of prior notice off that trace (Connecticut District Export Council).; step: 04; label: Scrub the export database; value: Step 4; detail: Test export records against hard-copy export documents. Remove foreign-to-foreign moves, cancelled orders and short shipments (International Trade Council).; step: 05; label: Stage a mock desk audit; value: Step 5; detail: Know where every record and data element lives before Customs asks. Most Customs checks are spot checks or desk reviews, and companies usually get caught on proof of exportation (KPMG US, International Trade Council).

text.title: Five Moves Before the First Drawback Claim
text.tspan: Five Moves Before the First Drawback Claim

rect.title: step: 01; label: Run the five-year lookback test; value: Step 1; detail: First-time claimants can reach back five years from import. Mid-sized companies that assume drawback is only for big companies find the number gets their CFO's attention (Evana).

text.title: First-time claimants can reach back five years from import. Mid-sized companies that assume drawback is only for big companies find the number gets their CFO's attention (Evana).

rect.title: step: 02; label: Weigh recovery against filing cost; value: Step 2; detail: If projected recovery does not beat the administrative expense of filing, do not file (Scarlett Jones). Specialist fees start around 10% of recovery (Nogueiras).

text.title: If projected recovery does not beat the administrative expense of filing, do not file (Scarlett Jones). Specialist fees start around 10% of recovery (Nogueiras).

rect.title: step: 03; label: Trace one shipment PO to export; value: Step 3; detail: Trace a single shipment from purchase order to import, through inventory and on to export. Customs grants waiver of prior notice off that trace (Connecticut District Export Council).

text.title: Trace one shipment PO to export
Trace a single shipment from purchase order to import, through inventory and on to export. Customs grants waiver of prior notice off that trace (Connecticut District Export Council).

rect.title: step: 04; label: Scrub the export database; value: Step 4; detail: Test export records against hard-copy export documents. Remove foreign-to-foreign moves, cancelled orders and short shipments (International Trade Council).

text.title: Test export records against hard-copy export documents. Remove foreign-to-foreign moves, cancelled orders and short shipments (International Trade Council).

rect.title: step: 05; label: Stage a mock desk audit; value: Step 5; detail: Know where every record and data element lives before Customs asks. Most Customs checks are spot checks or desk reviews, and companies usually get caught on proof of exportation (KPMG US, International Trade Council).

text.title: Know where every record and data element lives before Customs asks. Most Customs checks are spot checks or desk reviews, and companies usually get caught on proof of exportation (KPMG US, International Trade Council).

Assumptions: The order of steps follows the operator gates and pro-tips the practitioners cited. Customs refunds 99% of eligible duties, taxes and fees and keeps 1%, as International Tariff Management reports.
